newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Danone sees contribution outside Europe to double.
newsitem.headline: Danone sees contribution outside Europe to double.

text.p: French food giant Danone Group said on Tuesday it sees sales in Latin America, Central Asia and Asia doubling their contributions to the group's turnover by the year 2000.

"The turnover of the company outside Europe is 15 billion French Francs and we want to double the figure before the year 2000 to at least achieve 30 billion French Francs," chairman and chief executive Franck Riboud told Reuters at a news conference.
He said much of the growth would be organic but did not rule out future alliances.

"We are in a (business) world that is growing very fast. We have to look at any opportunity...I think it is very important to grow fast and the best way is to form alliances with people in that country," Riboud said.
Europe now contributes 85 percent of the group's turnover with regions outside Europe accouting for 15 percent. Riboud said Asia's turnover will exceed U.S. $1 billion this year.
Asia, in particularly India, Indonesia, China and Malaysia, is the key strategic area for Danone group because of its high population and increasing purchasing power, Riboud said.
Danone intends to push ahead in its core businesses of biscuits and dairy products in Asia, he said.

Riboud was confident that the company would be able to achieve its six percent growth projection in net profit for its fiscal year ending December 31 1996, despite the spate of bad weather which hit Europe in the third quarter.
"I am really confident with the six percent growth," he said. "At least six percent in net profit will be achieved."
He said while the poor weather had affected Danone's beer and mineral water sectors, the company's other activites would be able to cover the shortfall.
